name: lz77
description: A hardware LZ77/LZSS compressor (encoder) plus a matching decompressor (decoder), wired together as a self-checking loopback so the reconstructed byte stream equals the input.
authorship: Zero ASIC Corporation; author Andreas Olofsson

human_review.notes: Provenance (model and date) confirmed by the author; architecture, scope, and verification were directed and reviewed by the author.

spec.summary: Synthesizable, technology-agnostic LZ77/LZSS compressor codec. The benchmark top lz77 wires an encoder (lz77_enc) into a decoder (lz77_dec) as a loopback so the reconstructed byte stream equals the input. The encoder is a hash-based FPGA-compressor structure: a 4-byte multiplicative hash indexes a table holding the NWAY most-recent positions, candidates are extended in parallel over a 32 KB sliding window with a 64-byte parallel match-extend datapath, and the longest match >= MINMATCH wins (emitting a {len,dist} token) or else a literal token is emitted. The decoder reconstructs into a 32 KB circular output history, copying matched bytes back with overlap (RLE) support. The hash is only a hint: every candidate is verified by an explicit byte compare and gated by a legal distance, so the codec is lossless regardless of match quality. All sliding-window and table sizes are parameters (defaults: 32 KB window, WW=64 parallel compare, NWAY=4 candidates).
key_decisions: Use a hash-based match finder (4-byte multiplicative hash into an NWAY table) instead of a dynamic-index/content-addressed match finder, which avoids the catastrophic LUT blowup observed with the dynamic-index approach.
Store the hash table, the shared 32 KB compressor history, and the decoder's 32 KB output history in single-port la_spram BRAM (half the ASIC area of dual-port); probe candidates serially over NWAY.

Verify every hash candidate with an explicit byte compare and gate it by dist in [1, min(pos, WIN)] so a stale or aliased hash entry can never produce an invalid match -- it degrades to a literal, keeping the codec lossless.
Word-organize the history with byte-write enable so the two words covering any source byte read in a single cycle, enabling ~64 B/cycle on long matches.
Accept two ratio-only simplifications (never correctness): insert only the current position into the hash table each step, and check only NWAY candidates per bucket.
Handle the decoder dist==1 read-after-write hazard with a 1-deep write-forward on the synchronous-read output history BRAM.

origin.notes: Original implementation written for LogikBench; follows the cited algorithm/standard and hardware architectures, not copied from any specific HDL source.

references: J. Ziv and A. Lempel, 'A universal algorithm for sequential data compression,' IEEE Trans. Information Theory, vol. 23, no. 3, pp. 337-343, 1977. (LZ77)
J. A. Storer and T. G. Szymanski, 'Data compression via textual substitution,' Journal of the ACM, vol. 29, no. 4, pp. 928-951, 1982. (LZSS: explicit literal/match flagging)
DEFLATE Compressed Data Format Specification, RFC 1951, 1996. (hashed 3/4-byte match finding over a 32 KB window, as in zlib)
zlib deflate.c (J. Gailly, M. Adler) -- the hash-chain match finder (4-byte hash, recent-position chains) this design parallelizes.
M. S. Abdelfattah et al., 'Gzip on a chip: high performance lossless data compression on FPGAs using OpenCL,' IWOCL, 2014. (parallel windowed LZ77 match finding on FPGA)
